title: How Scale's Alexandr Wang approached TAM, customer success, and early pricing
summary: Alexandr Wang explains why Scale prioritized customer success over sales, let early customers shape the roadmap, and delayed pricing optimization. He argues market growth and ability to dominate matter more than TAM, and that startups die from self-inflicted mistakes rather than competition.

principles.text: Market growth rate and your odds of dominating it matter more than the size of the TAM.
principles.quote: It turns out, what matters actually more than that is that we’ve been able to dominate that TAM and because it’s growing really quickly, our company’s growing really quickly along with it.

principles.text: Ignore competitors and row your own race; startups die from self-inflicted errors like bad hires and wrong focus.
principles.quote: most startups don’t die because of competition but they die by suicide. Another way to put it that I think is good is, startups die of indigestion, not starvation.

principles.text: After your first customers, make your next hire customer success, not sales; happy customers become your acquisition channel.
principles.quote: it’s actually way better for your next hire for example, for there to be a customer success hire versus a sales hire because the reality is the sales piece is important but it’s far more important that you just build this culture of your customers loving you.

principles.text: Hire early customer success people from consulting backgrounds, not big-company CS, because startup CS is chaotic.
principles.quote: I think the profiles that actually are quite good are people with consulting backgrounds, in particular

principles.text: Pick your first customers carefully and let them dictate the roadmap, while digging into the pain to find a better solution.
principles.quote: you should really pick your first couple customers very well because no matter what, these first couple customers are going to define your product roadmap for the next while.

principles.text: Early on, don't optimize deal size; get customers who love the product, then raise prices once there's signal.
principles.quote: The only thing you should be focused on early is get customers who absolutely love you and know that they will pay for it but don’t be worried if they don’t pay too much very early on.
